description: Figure 5(b) displays the ratios of the loss values of different methods relative to Vanilla, plotted against FLOPs (floating-point operations). The x-axis, labeled “FLOPs,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^9 to 10^12, with tick marks at intervals of 10^9, 10^10, 10^11, and 10^12. The y-axis, labeled “Loss Ratio w.r.t FLOPs,” is linear and spans from 0 to 3.4, with tick marks at intervals of 0.4. The plot contains five distinct lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (purple solid line), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue dashed line), SepLLM (n=64) (orange solid line), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green solid line), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red solid line). All lines start at a loss ratio of approximately 3.4 when FLOPs is 10^9 and decrease as FLOPs increase. The Vanilla line remains relatively flat at a loss ratio of about 3.4. The StrmLLM (n=64) line shows a steep initial decline, reaching a loss ratio of approximately 2.7 at 10^12 FLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64) line starts at a loss ratio of about 3.0 and declines to approximately 2.6 at 10^12 FLOPs. The SepLLM (n=64, H) and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) lines begin at approximately 3.0 and 3.2 respectively, and both decrease to approximately 2.5 at 10^12 FLOPs.
